verdictHolds.reason: All four main commits' full file lists were cross-checked against the survey's files array: ins (2b4be7c: config.js, config.url-validation.test.js, add/controller.js, add/controller.test.js — 4/4), animals (b7c5039b: config.js, config.test.js, party-picker.controller.test.js — 3/3), tests (48ea0c0 + cd378de union: auth-state.ts, addresses-read-only.spec.ts, contact-address.spec.ts, environment.ts — 4/4). The one genuinely novel finding — fixtures/auth-state.ts's marker-free but semantically broken auto-merge — is independently confirmed by reading the trial-merge blob directly: the AuthTarget type has lost cookieName while the plants literal still sets it, and authCookieNameFor never reads it, so plants would silently fall back to 'sid' on the compose stack. The proposed per-target lookup fix is correct for ins and plants (verified against their own config.js isDevelopment-conditional cookie defaults) and rightly leaves animals untouched (its cookie name never varies by environment).

missed.statement: The resolution never states explicitly that no change is needed for the tests repo's 'e2e'/'admin' (animals) AUTH_TARGETS entries, or why: animals-frontend's own auth.cookieName config has no isDevelopment branch (always 'sid'), so the existing flat AUTH_COOKIE_NAME='sid' fallback is already correct on both the compose stack and CDP and the generalised lookup table rightly has no 'animals' entry. This was verified directly (src/config/config.js in trade-imports-animals-frontend) but the survey's resolution and its verdictWhy stop at 'ins, plants and animals' in the summary without showing the animals check, leaving a reader to wonder whether animals was actually considered or just assumed safe.
